title: 7.1.1 Arcade Cabinet (Q2 Synthesis)
description: Q2 synthesis: ship a game you designed. The checklist is the spec — twelve things the game must contain. Everything else is your call.

steps.title: Pitch your game in README.md before you write code
steps.instructions: A paragraph: what it is, how a player wins, how a player loses. Written first, so the rest of this list has something to serve.

steps.title: A class you wrote yourself, used to make at least two objects
A Group that manages many sprites at once
An overlap or a collision that changes the game
steps.instructions: Changes something a player would notice — score, health, a sprite disappearing. Two sprites bumping and nothing happening does not count.

steps.title: Motion you tuned on purpose
steps.instructions: Gravity, friction, bounciness, drag, velocity — pick what your game needs and set it to a value you chose, not the default.

steps.title: At least three game states, and a way to get between them
steps.instructions: Title, play, and game over is the usual three. Pause, win, and shop are all fair game too.

steps.title: Something that survives closing the tab
steps.instructions: storeItem to save it, getItem to read it back. A high score is the easy one; a save slot is more interesting.

steps.title: A function of your own that takes a parameter and returns a value
An array of game data that a loop reads
steps.instructions: Levels, waves, spawn points, dialogue lines — whatever your game has more than one of.

steps.title: Any two of: an animated sprite, a camera that follows, a joint, a pause state
steps.instructions: Pick the two that fit the game you pitched. Do not pick the two that are easiest to bolt on.

steps.title: Three PASS / FAIL tests of your own logic
steps.instructions: Call one of your functions with an input you know the answer to, and print PASS or FAIL.

steps.title: README, comments, and Appendix A style
steps.instructions: The README says how to play and what changed from your pitch and why. Appendix A applies to the code.

requirements.title: A class of your own
requirements.description: A class you declared yourself — any name, any purpose. The checker cannot tell whether you made two of them; the teacher reads for that.

requirements.title: A Group
requirements.description: A Group holding sprites you manage together

requirements.title: An overlap or collision
requirements.description: overlaps, collides, overlapping, or colliding between sprites or groups

requirements.title: Player input
requirements.description: Keyboard or mouse input the player uses to control the game

requirements.title: Motion tuned on purpose
requirements.description: gravity, friction, bounciness, drag, or a velocity you set yourself

requirements.title: Game states
requirements.description: A state variable set to a named state — 'title', 'play', 'gameover', or whatever you called yours. The checker cannot count your states; the teacher reads for three.

requirements.title: Saves and loads
requirements.description: storeItem writes it, getItem reads it back — both, or it does not survive the tab closing

requirements.title: A function that takes a parameter and returns a value
requirements.description: Your own function, with at least one parameter, that returns something. A named function, an arrow, or a method on your class all count.

requirements.title: An array of game data
requirements.description: An array you filled with more than one thing

requirements.title: A loop that reads it
requirements.description: for, for...of, or forEach — an array nobody loops over is just storage

requirements.title: Tests report PASS or FAIL
requirements.description: A check that prints PASS when it matches the known answer and FAIL when it does not. The checker cannot count your tests — three is on you, and the teacher reads for it.
